markdown_report:
**Recommendation:** retain fixed 0.5 terminal/reconstruction training and strengthen the reversible optimizer-transfer audit with matched zero-gradient controls and a directly measured mixture update. At 40% progress, prioritize this bounded diagnostic over adaptive weighting or additional training arms.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Equal branch coefficients do not establish equal optimization influence; sequence weighting, exposure and gradient magnitude differ. (2) Serving parity passed 67 cases/category, but missing SciPy interrupted diagnostics; residual evidence remains unavailable. (3) Electronics’ recent-deletion diagnostic hit@10 change was −0.125 [−0.21875, −0.046875]. This motivates terminal-prediction investigation without establishing objective conflict or validation benefit.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates examining reconstruction-to-terminal transfer. (2) [Task Affinity Grouping](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=hqDb8d65Vfh) measures hypothetical-update transfer, but optimizer history requires additional controls. (3) [AdamW documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.AdamW.html) distinguishes zero gradients from absent gradients; retained moments and decay can move parameters without a current objective gradient. (4) [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) limit interpretation beyond the pinned sampled protocol.

Three directions remain: objective alignment, diagnostic reliability and evaluation scope.

| Direction | Existing measurement | Remaining gap | Proposed addition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alignment | Weighting; gradient cosine | Optimizer history and nonlinear adaptation | Zero-controlled branch and mixture updates |
| Reliability | Sampler/export parity | Interrupted probes; incomplete rollback | Independent execution; continuation verification |
| Evaluation | Fixed sampled HR@10 | Generalization beyond candidates | Explicit scope and denominators |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more work.

- **Optimizer-transfer audit: 5/6/7.** Originality: adapts established affinity methods, without a new learning rule. Potential: identifies conditional local interactions, but cannot predict eventual HR@10. Difficulty: reuses losses, but transactional optimizer controls and continuation verification are substantial.
- **Target-count-controlled reconstruction audit: 3/6/4.** Originality: isolates supervision sampling, using standard subsampling. Potential: distinguishes variance from corruption effects, but retains target-location differences. Difficulty: preserve original corruption and sample one existing target; reproducible pairing requires care [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690).
- **Fault-validated diagnostic execution: 4/7/4.** Originality: adapts mutation testing, but remains infrastructure. Potential: exposes silent failures, without establishing ranking gains. Difficulty: temporary fixtures are small; coverage and false-alarm accounting require care [MDPMorph](https://valerio-terragni.github.io/assets/pdf/li-ase-2025.pdf).

**Selected algorithm.** Use one preregistered checkpoint and user-disjoint public update/assessment prefixes. Compare no-step, explicit-zero-gradient, half-scaled terminal, half-scaled reconstruction and actual mixture steps from identical transactional snapshots. Define conditional affinity as assessment loss after zero-step minus loss after objective-step. Separately report total change versus no-step, displacement, fixed-candidate margins and decay sensitivity.

```text
snapshot complete training state at an iteration boundary
cache paired update and disjoint assessment batches
for declared decay setting and update condition:
    restore snapshot; apply the specified gradient and clipping pipeline
    measure assessment loss, margins and displacement
restore snapshot; verify continuation against an audit-free replay
```

For the exposure control, retain every original MASK and supervise one uniformly selected original target. Its expected sequence-mean gradient equals all-target reconstruction; variance differs. Restoring other masks is a separate corruption control. Budget all work beforehand; retain one BERT4Rec/checkpoint per category, fixed training, host validation and predictor consistency. No audit-driven reweighting, validation-gain claim or inferred user intent is justified.

idea.description: Add a preregistered, transactional optimizer-transfer audit to fixed 0.5 terminal/reconstruction BERT4Rec training. Measure conditional effects of coefficient-scaled branch gradients and the actual mixture gradient against matched explicit-zero-gradient steps, while separately reporting total optimizer effects against a no-step baseline.
idea.motivation: The supplied evidence supports serving consistency and conditional history sensitivity, but supplies no objective-transfer measurement or validation gain. Gradient cosine and nominal coefficients omit optimizer history, clipping and finite-step adaptation. A no-step comparison alone also includes retained momentum and decay. Matched zero-gradient steps and direct mixture measurement make the local question interpretable without changing training or deploying another predictor. Exact continuation verification is a prerequisite for trusting a reversible audit.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the corrected BERT4Rec architecture, actual baseline loss, negative sampler, endpoint/window distribution, truncation and all-MASK corruption. Record the supplied reconstruction policy rather than replacing it with another paper's sampler. For fixed mixture training, assign exactly half of an even batch to each branch using a dedicated generator; average supervised target losses within each sequence, average sequences within branches, and use L=0.5*L_terminal+0.5*L_reconstruction. Equal coefficients do not equalize exposure or optimizer influence. Audit results never trigger reweighting, clipping changes, parameter repairs or category-specific objective selection.

Predeclare one checkpoint/update index, a small fixed audit batch count, user-disjoint update and assessment sets, eligible endpoints, candidate construction, decay settings, numerical thresholds, uncertainty procedure and diagnostic compute cap within the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Remaining budget and runtime are not supplied, so do not promise extra training arms or a step-size grid. Use the current learning rate as the primary step size; any additional step size must be declared and budgeted beforehand. Each category trains exactly one independent model. Temporary counterfactual updates are rolled back and never saved as alternative predictors, selected checkpoints or fused scores.

Cache audit batches using dedicated generators without advancing the training iterator. Select common public training windows under the supplied user/window distribution for branch comparisons. Terminal input uses the window's final item as label, retains at most maxlen-1 preceding items, appends reserved MASK and excludes later interactions. Reconstruction retains the supplied window and complete original corruption. Record any unavoidable mismatch in window/context construction. Assessment uses user-disjoint terminal prefixes, unchanged loss type, fixed negatives and fixed eligible candidate sets across all counterfactuals. Candidate eligibility depends only on the complete preceding prefix, never later events. This controls paired comparisons without making reconstruction and terminal target positions or right context equivalent.

At an iteration boundary with no live backward graph, deep-copy model and optimizer state dictionaries. Separately snapshot every parameter's gradient, preserving None versus explicit zero; each module's individual training flag; scheduler and GradScaler state when present; Python, NumPy, Torch CPU/CUDA RNGs; every explicit generator; sampler/iterator state if touched; and mutable module state absent from state_dict. Uncopied state dictionaries retain tensor references and are insufficient. Preserve parameter identity by restoring model state in place. Do not audit between an unfinished AMP backward/unscale/step cycle; use a boundary before forward or after scaler.update().

For each paired audit batch, restore identical weights, buffers, optimizer moments, step counters and all other state before every condition. The primary conditions are NO_STEP, ZERO_GRADIENT_STEP, HALF_TERMINAL, HALF_RECONSTRUCTION and MIXTURE. Compute g_T and g_R from declared branch sequence means. HALF_TERMINAL supplies 0.5*g_T, HALF_RECONSTRUCTION supplies 0.5*g_R, and MIXTURE supplies 0.5*g_T+0.5*g_R before the actual training clipping pipeline. Measure MIXTURE directly: Adam's nonlinear adaptation means branch parameter updates cannot be averaged or added to reconstruct it. Full-strength standalone branch steps are optional secondary controls, explicitly distinguished from half-scaled ablations and included only if preregistered and affordable.

Define a common intended active parameter set for paired conditions. For ZERO_GRADIENT_STEP, explicitly assign zero tensors to those parameters; zero_grad(set_to_none=False) does not allocate gradients where none exist. For objective conditions, represent missing gradients as zeros on the same set, and keep parameters outside it at None consistently. Record natural gradient-support differences and any resulting deviation from the actual training pipeline. If support differs in a meaningful way, add a separately labeled faithful-pipeline mixture comparison or mark exact training-update correspondence unavailable. Do not silently treat None and zero as equivalent. Apply the same optimizer parameter groups, current moments/counters, learning rate, precision policy, clipping rule and weight decay to matched conditions.

Run primary counterfactuals with decay enabled exactly as configured in training, plus a small preregistered decay-disabled set with matched zero controls to assess sensitivity. AdamW decay acts separately from moments; ordinary Adam's coupled decay enters moments. Disabling decay for the current Adam step does not remove historical decay contributions. Describe the effect as conditional on optimizer history, not a history-free gradient effect. Use eval mode and float32 with autograd enabled for the primary controlled audit, declaring its difference from stochastic or AMP training. If invoked inside a no_grad adapter, wrap forward/loss/gradient computation in torch.enable_grad(). If inference mode is active, also enter torch.inference_mode(False) and recreate or clone inference-created inputs inside that context.

For each decay setting, define A_c=L_assessment(after matched zero-gradient step)-L_assessment(after condition c); positive values indicate a locally beneficial conditional current-gradient contribution. Also report total loss change relative to NO_STEP, raw pre/post losses, and relative transfer Z=1-L_after/L_no_step only when its denominator exceeds a preregistered threshold. Z describes the entire update and must not be relabeled as zero-controlled affinity. Report direct MIXTURE-versus-HALF_TERMINAL and MIXTURE-versus-HALF_RECONSTRUCTION loss differences; these are conditional finite-update comparisons, not additive decompositions. Report per-block parameter displacement, raw/coefficient-scaled gradient norms, clipping factors, target counts, loss denominators and elapsed GPU time. Count tied parameters once. Target-minus-tenth-negative margins use fixed sets of one target and 99 unique eligible negatives; insufficient candidates or invalid denominators yield unavailable values with reasons. These are training-prefix diagnostics, not host validation.

For a supervision-count control, run the supplied reconstruction sampler unchanged to produce corrupted input x and nonempty target set M. Sample j uniformly within each sequence's M using a dedicated generator; keep every MASK in x and supervise only j. Compare sequence means L_all=(1/|M|)*sum(loss_i) and L_one=loss_j, then average sequences. Conditional on x and M, expected losses and gradients agree, but sampling variance differs; nonlinear optimizer steps need not agree in expectation. A global target average changes sequence weights, and summed targets change loss scale. If budget permits a separate corruption control, restore the other masked positions from the cached original window while retaining j as MASK; label that comparison as changing visible context. Do not call one-target/original-corruption a published one-mask ablation or a complete exposure match to terminal learning.

Summarize fixed paired batches with explicit counts and raw outcomes. Predeclare any paired bootstrap unit and resample count; user-level or user-clustered resampling must respect repeated windows. Intervals remain descriptive, conditional on checkpoint, seed, optimizer history, candidate construction and selected users. No multiplicity-adjusted discovery claim follows from exploratory block or condition comparisons. One-step training-loss benefit cannot establish convergence, recovered intent or future macro HR@10.

Restore all captured state in finally blocks, removing audit hooks and restoring module modes individually. Restore RNGs last, after any restoration operation that could consume randomness. Require exact model and optimizer restoration and verify scheduler/scaler, gradients including None, buffers, explicit generators and tracked mutable state. Restoration failure stops training continuation. State loading cannot undo tensor version counters, external hook side effects or untracked iterator changes, so structural safeguards remain necessary.

Before trusting the audit, perform a small budgeted continuation check: from one snapshot, replay identical cached training batches with and without the audit under deterministic execution, and compare losses, gradients, parameters, buffers, optimizer/scheduler/scaler state and subsequent RNG states exactly. Restore the original snapshot afterward. Use the actual training mode and AMP pipeline for this continuation check when applicable. A passing check establishes numerical continuation only for that tested path. If exact equality is unsupported or fails, report the audit unavailable and diagnose the mismatch rather than claiming harmless rollback or silently relaxing tolerances.

Repair missing SciPy usage with dependency-free implementations of the specific required statistics or mark only the dependent probe unavailable. Execute diagnostic probes independently, preserving completed measurements and recording exceptions, skipped probes, dependency failures and actual hook invocation counts. Residual-patching availability must report the actual failure stage rather than a stale sampler/parity gate message. Prioritize a small clean-control and deliberately injected-fault verification of the audit and status reporting before adding expensive residual interventions; report detected/eligible faults and false alarms with denominators. Fixtures never modify the deployed model or benchmark evaluator.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), view.model as the actual trained module, all ModelView interfaces, actual category identity, family-specific sample_batch and B x L loader tensors. Preserve existing embedding, margin, sampler, serving-parity and behavioral measurements with their definitions and availability limits. Restore diagnostic model and RNG state. Keep serialization identity and exported-serving checks across short, full-length, truncated and batched inputs; failed parity blocks interpretation of serving-sensitive probes.

Keep Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch; single-GPU execution; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; and trial-local artifacts. Serving retains maxlen-1 history items, appends reserved MASK and reads its actual final nonpadding position, never count-1. Preserve bidirectional masked-target training without shifted-target leakage. Each category loads exactly one checkpoint; synchronize checkpoint configuration and predictor writer. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five designated real training users per category. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable review fields, product attributes and simulator traits remain unobserved.

Select solely using the unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10 with its pinned users, candidates and seed. Do not infer full-catalog performance from sampled HR@10, use diagnostic batches as validation labels, tune repeatedly on audit assessment users, add popularity/transition scores, or read other trials and checkpoints. Item frequency, target location and position patterns remain possible shortcuts; paired controls narrow interpretations without proving semantic reasoning. Report every failed diagnostic and its compute cost. Leave held-out evaluation to the host.
idea.pseudocode:
train one corrected BERT4Rec per category with the fixed half mixture
at a preregistered iteration boundary with no live backward graph:
    snapshot = deep_copy_complete_training_state()
    batches = cache_diagnostic_batches_without_advancing_training_iterator()
    # Update and assessment users are disjoint; negatives and candidates are fixed.
    try:
        for paired_batch in preregistered_batches:
            original_x, M = unchanged_reconstruction_sampler(paired_batch.window)
            j = uniformly_select_one_original_target_per_sequence(M)
            # Keep original_x unchanged for the one-target exposure control.
            for decay_setting in preregistered_decay_settings:
                for condition in [NO_STEP, ZERO, HALF_T, HALF_R, MIXTURE,
                                  ONE_TARGET_R_WITH_ORIGINAL_CORRUPTION]:
                    restore_complete_snapshot_in_place(snapshot)
                    restore_all_rng_states_last()
                    enter inference_mode(False) and enable_grad()
                    recreate_inputs_if_needed(); model.eval()
                    if condition != NO_STEP:
                        assign consistent active-gradient support
                        if condition == ZERO:
                            explicitly_allocate_zero_gradients()
                        else:
                            compute declared sequence-mean losses
                            form specified coefficient-scaled gradient
                            # MIXTURE uses the summed gradient before clipping.
                        apply actual declared clipping and optimizer step
                    measure terminal assessment loss, fixed-candidate margins,
                            gradient/clipping statistics and parameter displacement
            record zero-controlled affinity and total change versus NO_STEP
            record direct mixture-versus-scaled-branch differences
        summarize paired outcomes, availability, denominators and compute
    finally:
        restore complete snapshot in place; remove audit hooks
        restore each module mode and gradients including None
        restore RNG states last
        assert exact restoration of every captured state

verify a small deterministic continuation replay with versus without the audit
# Compare actual training losses, gradients, states and subsequent RNG states.
restore original snapshot; stop continuation on failed restoration
resume unchanged training only after required checks pass
save one category checkpoint with matching embedded predictor
submit through unchanged host validation; leave held-out evaluation to host

originality.positive: Combines established task-affinity measurement with optimizer-history controls, direct mixture updates and corruption-preserving supervision controls in serving-aligned BERT4Rec.
originality.negative: The constituent methods and optimizer equations are established; the contribution is a controlled diagnostic adaptation rather than a new learning algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can produce falsifiable local objective-interaction hypotheses and distinguish current-gradient contributions from retained optimizer dynamics.
future_potential.negative: Checkpoint-specific one-step loss effects may not predict ranking gains, and a reliable transactional implementation may consume budget better spent on simpler controlled training comparisons.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing model, losses and optimizer while leaving deployed inference unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Gradient-support semantics, exact restoration, AMP and generator state, independent probe execution and deterministic continuation verification make this substantially more difficult than a basic virtual update.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for BERT4Rec
contributions: Identifies weak correspondence between masked reconstruction and next-item prediction.
Motivates preserving and documenting the sampling distribution when studying objective transfer.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this fixed mixture or diagnostic.
Its sampling policy must not silently replace the corrected host sampler.

related_work.title: Task Affinity Grouping
contributions: Measures task interaction through hypothetical updates and changes in another task's loss.
limitations: Local transfer does not guarantee long-term ranking gains.
The proposed matched zero-gradient optimizer controls are an adaptation, not an established result from this reference.

related_work.title: MDPMorph
contributions: Combines metamorphic relations with model mutations to assess fault detection.
limitations: Provides no measured fault-detection or false-alarm rates for this BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes that sampled recommendation metrics can produce inconsistent model comparisons.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator or extrapolating its results to full-catalog ranking.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and appended-mask next-item inference.
Includes a one-mask ablation that changes corruption as well as supervision count.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed corruption-preserving target-subsampling control or its benefit on this benchmark.
Terminal supervision is already part of BERT4Rec's methodological context and should not be claimed as new.

related_work.title: PyTorch AdamW documentation
contributions: Documents moment updates, step counters and decoupled weight decay.
Explains why optimizer state and explicit zero versus absent gradients matter for counterfactual steps.
limitations: Optimizer equations support the control design but provide no empirical recommendation-transfer result.

related_work.title: PyTorch Adam documentation
contributions: Documents adaptive moment updates and coupled weight-decay behavior in ordinary Adam.
limitations: Disabling current-step decay does not remove its historical contributions to stored moments.

related_work.title: PyTorch Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Documents model and optimizer checkpoint state and the need to copy state dictionaries when preserving snapshots.
limitations: State dictionaries alone do not capture gradients, module modes, all randomness, iterator mutations or external side effects.

related_work.title: PyTorch Optimizer.zero_grad documentation
contributions: Distinguishes None gradients from zero tensors and their optimizer consequences.
limitations: Calling zero_grad with set_to_none=False does not allocate every missing gradient required by an explicit-zero control.

related_work.title: PyTorch Automatic Mixed Precision Recipe
contributions: Documents GradScaler state and appropriate AMP checkpoint boundaries.
limitations: A float32 evaluation-mode audit differs from an AMP training update and must be labeled accordingly.

related_work.title: PyTorch Generator documentation
contributions: Provides explicit generator state capture and restoration needed for reproducible sampling.
limitations: Restoring generators does not restore untracked sampler positions or external random sources.

related_work.title: PyTorch Autograd Mechanics
contributions: Distinguishes default gradient mode, no-grad mode and inference mode.
Supports correctly enabling counterfactual gradient computation inside diagnostic adapters.
limitations: Enabling gradients alone does not neutralize inference-mode tensor restrictions or guarantee reversible execution.
